title: indigo_agent_scheduler: make the hourly Sun and Moon grid rebuild cheaper, it takes about 100 ms (0.5-1 s on a Raspberry Pi)
description:
Performance follow-up from the scheduler performance study (scratchpad perf/, i5-9400, -O3; Raspberry Pi 4 about 5-10x slower).

indigo_scheduler_sky_build() takes about 100 ms (about 0.5-1 s on a Pi), 99 % in the full ELP2000 Moon theory (indigocat_moon_equatorial_coords, precision 0) called 49 times, and runs every hour on the agent queue.

Two options, the owner chooses before implementation:
1. Reuse Sun and Moon samples across the hourly rebuild: the grid start normally moves by exactly 3600 s, so 48 of 49 hourly samples are the same instants; keep them in the grid and look them up by exact time. Hourly rebuild 100 ms -> 2.3 ms; the first build and a delayed tick stay about 100 ms. Not bit-identical: up to 2e-6 deg Sun altitude and 1.5e-6 Moon illumination, because indigocat_get_nutation() keeps a process-global cache of the last epoch (LN_NUTATION_EPOCH_THRESHOLD 0.1 day, indigocat_nutation.c), so today's grid already depends on call history. Prototype: perf/proto_B_solar_cache.diff.
2. Lower the Moon precision: indigocat_moon_equatorial_coords_prec(jd, &m, 0.0001) is 40x faster for every build, error <= 33 arcsec, far below the Moon parallax (up to 1 deg) the grid already ignores; a deliberate change of results.

Side finding to check: the static nutation cache in indigocat_nutation.c is not synchronised across threads.
